speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs with regard to the rising Internet love scams that resulted in $37 million of losses in 2017 (a) what is the typical profile of these victims; (b) what has been done to raise awareness of such scams to this group; and (c) what plans does the Ministry have to further reduce the risk of Singaporeans being cheated by such Internet love scams.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Police have been working with partners, such as the National Crime Prevention Council (NCPC), to step up public education on Internet Love Scams.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We put out advisory messages through multiple platforms, including newspapers, television, roadshows, posters on public transport, and social media.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We have also set up an Anti-Scam Helpline 1800-722-6688, and we also have the www.scamalert.sg website.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: A significant proportion of Internet Love Scams are committed remotely by foreign syndicates.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Police will continue to work closely with foreign law enforcement counterparts to crack down on overseas syndicates targeting Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Police also work with Facebook to take down accounts that are used by scam syndicates.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We intend to engage other major social media companies to do the same.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I think such Love Scams have been around for quite a number of years and it is quite worrying that people continue to fall prey to these scams.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope the Police can review the effectiveness of our Public Education programmes and see whether we can do more to prevent people from falling for such scams.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: One, with reference to such Internet Love Scams, how much money has actually been recovered by the Police and returned to the victims?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Two, many of the victims, in particular, those who may have lost their entire life savings to such scams would be significantly affected, both financially and mentally, especially those who are more aged.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Are there any forms of assistance, such as counselling, provided for such victims to aid in their recovery?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: If not, are there any plans to have such forms of assistance?

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We share the Member's concern on Internet Love Scams and would like to assure the hon Member that we will continuously review our outreach strategies and ensure their effectiveness.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: However, I should emphasise that the nature of Internet Love Scams is such that they are typically borderless and involves transnational syndicates.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: But nonetheless, we will try our very best to review our strategies and strengthen our coordination with international agencies as well as other countries' police forces.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: On the issue of support, there are various places where victims can seek support.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Social service organisations are one, grassroots organisations as well as Family Service Centres are others.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: I should, however, emphasise that prevention is always better than cure, and it is important to heed the Police's educational messages.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: One simple message is not to send money to people whom we do not know well.
